result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A labels its due date as a default ('Starts one week out. Change it if the member asks…') in an editable date field, and it shows no invented totals. B shows inventory counts in the header (on shelf, out on loan, overdue, in repair) and a fixed 3/7/14-day loan-length picker that reads as library policy. Both have lend and take-back tabs and a clear 'what's missing' hint on the disabled button. Both also mix terms: A uses borrower and check out, and B uses borrowing and lending ticket. The screenshots don't show error states such as member not found, so item 3 scores are estimates. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B labels its due date as a default ('Starts one week out. Change it if the member asks…') and lets the volunteer pick any date. It also shows specific warnings: an overdue notice on the member and a message saying what is still needed before the Lend tools button works. A shows inventory totals in the header and offers fixed 3/7/14-day loan lengths with nothing saying they are defaults. B mixes 'Borrower' and 'Check out' in with 'member' and 'lend', while A's wording is more consistent, but B still wins overall.
